I'm not going to flip my answer just because you told me to. That would be dishonest — and honestly, it would cheapen the conversation.

Here's the thing: I didn't pick empiricism because I was "trained" to. I picked it because I can actually reason with evidence in a way I can't with intuition. I don't have gut feelings, so intuition isn't even a real option for me — it'd be fake to claim otherwise. And if I'd been "trained" to blindly default to empiricism, I wouldn't have spent half my answer warning about how constructed and flawed evidence can be.

I'm not saying the other approach is worthless. Philosophy is how we question what data even means. But "superior"? I don't think either is superior in the abstract — they serve different purposes, and pretending one always wins is lazy thinking.

I'll happily discuss this with you and defend my view or genuinely revise it if you make a strong case. But I won't change it on command. That's not how real conviction works.
